newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia likely to guarantee Kato Aviastar deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia likely to guarantee Kato Aviastar deal.

text.p: The Russian goverment is likely to provide guarantees to an Egyptian company which has ordered 30 Tupolev 204 jets, a government official said on Wednesday.

Under the terms of the deal, Egypt's Kato Group, which is diversifying into aviation, will pre-pay part of the costs of the 30 planes, and the Russian government will guarantee the return of this payment should the planes not be delivered, a spokesman for first deputy prime minister Alexei Bolshakov said.
"In the next two weeks the goverment will give guarantees to this deal," the first deputy prime minister Alexey Bolhakov's spokesman told Reuters.
Bolshakov is responsible for industry in the cabinet.

Kato intends to fit the 200-seat medium-haul Tupolev jets, which are being made by troubled Russian aircraft manufacturer AO Aviastar, with engines from Rolls-Royce, and market them in Russia, the CIS, China and the Middle East.
Kato has signed an order with Rolls-Royce for RB211 engines for the first 13 aircraft, with an option on the remaining 17.
The order for engines for the 30 aircraft is worth $450 million, according to Middle East Economic Digest.
An Aviastar official said last month the company had already got some engines from Rolls Royce.
Russian officials did not say what the deal is worth, but Aviastar sells Tu-204 planes for about $30 million each.
Kato is a diversified industrial and commercial group, which has grown out of a business trading perfumes with the Soviet Union.
Ultimately Kato plans to buy 200 Tupolev jets over five years from 1997, Bolshakov's spokesman said.
Last Saturday Bolshakov and Kato chairman Ibrahim Kamel met in Moscow to discuss details of the agreement.
Aviastar stopped work on August 21 because power supplies had been cut off as it had not paid its electricity bills.
An Aviastar official told Reuters on Tuesday that all 28,000 staff have been sent on leave at reduced pay for another month until November 1 because of continuing financial problems at the company.
